allowedSourceMaterial.overview: Ebenezer Scrooge is far too greedy to understand that Christmas is a time for kindness and generosity. But with the guidance of some new found friends, Scrooge learns to embrace the spirit of the season. A retelling of the classic Dickens tale with Disney's classic characters.

facts.title: Mickey's Christmas Carol

visibleEditorialCopy.curiosityHook: Can a stubborn miser truly change his ways before the season passes him by?
visibleEditorialCopy.description: Blinded by greed, Ebenezer Scrooge rejects the spirit of Christmas until newfound visitors arrive to guide him toward kindness in this animated retelling of the classic Dickens story starring iconic Disney characters.
visibleEditorialCopy.vibeSummary: Light, thoughtful, and comfortably paced for an easy family-friendly holiday viewing.
visibleEditorialCopy.whyWatch: At a breezy twenty-five minutes, Burny Mattinson's animated adaptation pairs timeless holiday sentiment with beloved classic characters for a gentle, family-friendly watch.

sourceEvidence.notes: description: Ebenezer Scrooge, the greed, the failure to grasp Christmas kindness, guidance from 'new found friends', the retelling of the classic Dickens tale, and the Disney characters all restate the overview. 'Blinded by greed' and 'rejects the spirit of Christmas' are figurative paraphrases of 'far too greedy to understand'. 'Iconic' for 'classic' echoes the tolerated 'iconic allies'. 'Animated' matches genre Animation. 'Guide him toward kindness' restates the overview's stated arc, which is part of the premise as the source frames it.

description: 'newfound visitors arrive' is a mild terminology shift from 'new found friends'. It keeps the 'newfound' qualifier and the guiding role. 'Visitors' and 'arrive' add a light concretization of how the guides enter Scrooge's story, but they name no identity, ghost, or mechanism. This is discussed under uncertaintyNotes.

curiosityHook: 'stubborn miser' is a characterization consistent with 'far too greedy'. 'Change his ways' echoes 'learns to embrace the spirit of the season'. 'Before the season passes him by' is figurative urgency in the same class as the tolerated 'before mom returns'. As an interrogative it asserts no event or outcome beyond the overview's own framing.

'Twenty-five minutes' matches runtimeMinutes=25. 'Beloved classic characters' is a light evaluative variant of 'Disney's classic characters'.

acceptedSemanticClassification: 'Light' matches emotionalWeight=light, 'thoughtful' matches moods, 'comfortably paced' matches pace=medium, 'easy' and 'breezy' match attentionDemand=easy, and 'family-friendly' matches situations=[family, easy-watch]. 'Gentle' and 'timeless holiday sentiment' are low-risk tonal shorthand.

claudeAdvisory.uncertaintyNotes: The only near-threshold item is 'newfound visitors arrive' in place of the source's 'new found friends'. It slightly recasts the relationship (friends versus visitors) and adds an arrival motion the overview does not state. It does not name the guides, assert a supernatural mechanism, or change what a viewer would expect from a family Christmas Carol retelling, so I keep it within tolerance. A stricter adjudicator could ask for 'friends' to be restored, in which case it would be a MINOR alias substitution. 'Stubborn' is an unsupported characterization flourish but not a plot claim.
